districtFact: Spokane Public Schools serves approximately 29,000 students across 58 schools in the Inland Northwest. SPS schedules Launch Conferences before regular classes and publishes year-specific opening dates for grades 1-12 and kindergarten; preschool programs may follow separate schedules. Most instructional Mondays begin one hour late for staff collaboration. Beginning in 2026-2027, SPS uses a 180-day balanced calendar with school breaks in October and February while retaining summer vacation.

about.title: About Spokane Public Schools
about.content: Spokane Public Schools is a preschool-through-grade-12 district headquartered at 200 N. Bernard in Spokane. District materials describe an organization of about 29,000 students, 58 schools, and more than 6,000 employees, making the school calendar a major planning reference across Spokane and the Inland Northwest.

about.title: Launch Conferences Come Before Classes
about.content: SPS schedules Launch Conferences before regular classes begin. Opening schedules can differ by grade level and school year, so families should use the dates listed for the specific year.

about.title: Balanced Calendar Starts in 2026–27
about.content: The 2025-2026 year follows SPS's earlier pattern. For 2026-2027 and 2027-2028, SPS and the Spokane Education Association adopted a balanced calendar with 180 instructional days, a shorter summer, and school breaks in October and February. SPS explicitly says this is not year-round school.

about.title: Most Mondays Use Collaboration Time
about.content: The calendar shades most instructional Mondays as Late Start/Collaboration days. The district says most students begin one hour later on Monday, but exact school hours and program exceptions matter. Holidays, PLID days, and balanced-calendar breaks interrupt the pattern, so families should use the year-specific Monday list rather than assume every Monday is identical.

about.title: Static PDF and Live Updates Can Differ
about.content: The one-page PDFs establish the published year pattern, while later district announcements may provide newer or more detailed program information. At the end of 2025-2026, for example, an SPS June update gave different preschool completion dates. This page records the discrepancy and uses the later official announcement for the affected program dates.

planningTips.title: Spokane Public Schools Calendar Notes
content: Do not treat Launch Conferences as the first regular day of classes. They are scheduled preparation and relationship-building dates before classes begin.
Match the opening date to the program: grades 1-12, kindergarten groups, all kindergarten together, PreK, and half-day or specialized preschool can differ.
Plan for most instructional Mondays to begin one hour late, then verify the student's school hours and any program exception.
For 2026-2027 and 2027-2028, account for the October and February balanced-calendar breaks in addition to Winter and Spring Break.
Treat PLID dates as non-student days. PLID means Professional Learning Improvement Day in SPS calendar terminology.
Weather/Emergency Make-Up dates remain no-school or outside-year reserves unless SPS explicitly activates them.
Use the live district announcements for final preschool, last-day, transportation, meal-service, and weather details because those can be updated after the PDF is published.

districtFaqs.q: Is Spokane Public Schools changing to year-round school?
districtFaqs.a: No. SPS calls the 2026-2027 and 2027-2028 model a balanced calendar, not year-round school. Students still have summer vacation and 180 instructional days, with school breaks in October and February.

districtFaqs.q: Do Spokane students start classes during Launch Conferences?
districtFaqs.a: Launch Conferences are scheduled before regular classes begin. The grade levels included and the opening sequence can vary by school year, so families should use the dates published for the specific year and school.

districtFaqs.q: Does SPS start late every Monday?
districtFaqs.a: Most instructional Mondays are one-hour late-start collaboration days, but holidays, no-school days, and breaks create exceptions. Exact clock times also differ by school and program.

districtFaqs.q: What is a PLID day in Spokane Public Schools?
districtFaqs.a: PLID is SPS's Professional Learning Improvement Day designation. Calendar dates labeled PLID/Non Student Day are staff learning or work days with no student attendance.

districtFaqs.q: Are SPS weather make-up days automatically school days?
districtFaqs.a: No. They are reserve dates and remain non-student or outside the scheduled year unless SPS activates them after a closure. Families should confirm any activation through a district announcement.
